questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The main function of bulliform cells in grasses is :
options: to make the leaf impermeable to fungal spores.
to minimize water loss during water stress.
questions.solution:
Bulliform cells are large, empty, colourless cells present on the adaxial epidermis of grass leaves.

When water is abundant, these cells absorb water, become turgid, and cause the leaf surface to be exposed.

During water stress, they lose turgor pressure and become flaccid, which makes the leaves curl inwards to minimize water loss.

Answer: to minimize water loss during water stress.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R:

Assertion A: Late wood has fewer xylary elements with narrow vessels.

Reason R: Cambium is less active in winters.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Assertion is false but Reason is true
Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false
questions.solution:
The activity of cambium is under the control of many physiological and environmental factors. Such activity can be observed in the form of annual rings.

In temperate regions, the climatic conditions are not uniform through the year.

  • In the spring, cambium is very active and produces a large number of xylary elements having vessels with wider cavities. The wood formed is called early wood or spring wood.
  • In winter, the cambium is less active and forms fewer xylary elements that have narrow vessels. The wood formed is called late wood or autumn wood.

questions.q:
In old trees the greater part of secondary xylem is dark brown and resistant to insect attack due to:
(a) secretion of secondary metabolites and their deposition in the lumen of vessels.
(b) deposition of organic compounds like tannins and resins in the central layers of stem.
(c) deposition of suberin and aromatic substances in the outer layer of stem.
(d) deposition of tannins, gum, resin and aromatic substances in the peripheral layers of stem.
(e) presence of parenchyma cells, functionally active xylem elements and essential oils.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: In old trees, the greater part of secondary xylem is dark brown due to deposition of organic compounds like tannins, resins, oils, gums, aromatic substances and essential oils in the central or innermost layers of the stem. These substances make it hard, durable and resistant to the attacks of microorganisms and insects. This region comprises dead elements with highly lignified walls and is called heartwood.

• During secondary growth in stem, meristematic tissue called cork cambium develops, usually in the cortex region. Phellogen is a couple of layers thick.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Endarch and exarch are the terms often used for describing the position of secondary xylem in the plant body.

Statement II: Exarch condition is the most common feature of the root system.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II arre true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.
questions.solution:
Primary xylem is of two types – protoxylem and metaxylem.

Arrangement of protoxylem and metaxylem:

  • In stems, the protoxylem lies towards the centre (pith) and the metaxylem lies towards the periphery of the organ. This type of primary xylem is called endarch.
  • In roots, the protoxylem lies towards periphery and metaxylem lies towards the centre. Such arrangement of primary xylem is called exarch.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Phloem in gymnosperms lacks:
options: Both sieve tubes and companion cells
questions.solution: Sieve elements are the chief conducting elements of the phloem which are of two types: sieve cells and sieve-tube members. Pores in sieve cells are narrow, there is seemingly uniformity in the structure of sieve areas and are found to be distributed evenly on all walls. The presence of sieve plates in sieve-tube members is one of the principal differences between sieve cells (absent) and sieve-tube members. In most gymnosperms and seedless vascular plants, sieve cells are the only kind of food-conducting cells whereas sieve-tube members are present in angiosperms. Sieve tubes are made of sieve tube members arranged terminally to one another.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the statements given below is not true about the formation of annual rings in trees?
options: Annual ring is a combination of spring wood and autumn wood produced in a year.
Differential activity of cambium causes light and dark bands of tissue - early and late wood respectively.
Activity of cambium depends upon variation in climate.
Annual rings are not prominent in trees of temperate region.
questions.solution: The activity of cambium is non-uniform in plants growing in regions of favorable climatic conditions (rainy or spring season) that alternate regularly with unfavorable climatic conditions (dry hot summer or cold winter). In temperate climates, the cambium is more active giving rise to a higher number of vessels with greater activities, while in winter, it becomes less active and forms narrower and smaller vessels. Both spring and autumn wood contribute for an annual ring, forming one ring a year. Annual rings are prominent in trees of temperate region.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Identify the wrong statement in the context of heartwood.
options: Organic compounds are deposited in it
It conducts water and minerals efficiently
It comprises dead elements with highly lignified walls
questions.solution: Heartwood is physiologically inactive due to the deposition of organic compounds and tyloses formation, so this will not conduct water and minerals. Heartwood is the central cylinder found in tree trunks. Heartwood forms as the tree ages, and the inner xylem cells lose the capacity to transmit water. Heartwood tends to be darker in colour than sapwood since it is normally filled with various types of oils, dyes, and sugars. The primary function of heartwood is to provide adequate support to the tree.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Cortex is the region found between:
questions.solution:
Cortex is the region present between epidermis and stele. The term cortex refers to the outermost layer of cells on a plant's stem or root. The cortex has the ability to transport nutrients into the core of the root. It uses diffusion to achieve transport. It also stores nutrients in the form of starch.

The cortex acts as a protective covering on plant and is often waterproof. Depending on the type of plant, the cortex can also store carbohydrates, tannins, essential oils, and resins.

questions.q: Specialized epidermal cells surrounding the guard cells are called:
questions.solution: As subsidiary cells and guard cells both are the modification of epidermal cells in which guard cells have chloroplasts which is absent in surrounding subsidiary cells. Subsidiary cells are the accessory cells to guard cells in the epidermis of plants. Two or four subsidiary cells are found surrounding the pair of guard cells. Subsidiary cells do not consist of chloroplasts. They provide support for the functioning of guard cells in the epidermis. Subsidiary cells play a role in ion channel-mediated opening and closing of guard cells.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The balloon-shaped structures called tyloses
options: Originate in the lumen of vessels
Are extensions of xylem parenchyma cells into vessels
Are linked to the ascent of sap through xylem vessels
questions.solution:
Tyloses are balloon-shaped structures in xylem vessels developed by xylem parenchyma cells.



Malpighi (1686) for the first time reported the ‘balloon-shaped sacs’ in the lumen of vessels of heartwood and he named it as tyloses based on the Greek word ‘Thyllen’ meaning ‘bag’ or ‘container’. Tyloses development occurs through the pit-pairs connecting parenchyma and tracheids or vessels. Sometimes many tyloses originate from a single parenchymatous cell. The tyloses completely fill the lumen rich in the tracheids and vessels of heartwood than sapwood.

options: A bundle sheath surrounds each bundle.
There are no vessels with perforations.
Xylem is surrounded all around by phloem.

questions.solution: The tracheary elements comprise tracheids and vessels. The main function is the conduction of sap. Tracheids differ from other tracheary elements in being imperforate, comparatively short, and single-celled. While the vessels are longer and multi celled.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Meristematic tissue responsible for increase in girth of tree trunk is:
questions.solution:
Lateral meristem are present along the lateral sides of stem and roots, and are responsible for lateral growth of trees. Intercalary meristem is associated with the growth in length in the middle position, causing internodal elongation. Phellogen also known as cork cambium is the meristematic plant tissue responsible for the formation of the periderm. Apical meristem is involved in the growth region in plants found within the root tips and the tips of the new shoots and leaves.
Related Theory
When plant breeders want to re-generate plants that are virus-free using asexual multiplication (in order to obtain clones of the primary unhealthy plant), they often collect the apical meristem from the infected plant, and cultivate it in appropriate media, so that a new, complete and virus-free plantlets develop. High metabolic processes (Enzyme activity); High concentration of auxin and Cytokinin hormone (Low pH); Cell multiplication very high and plasmodesmata size very small which prevent the movement of the virus from one cell to another cell.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which part would be most suitable for raising virus-free plants for micropropagation?
questions.solution: Generally, it is believed that actively growing regions of plants (i.e., shoot apex and root apex) do not have viruses. Due to this big advantage, these regions are used in the production of virus free plants through meristem culture technique. In meristem culture explants are taken from shoot apex or shoot apical meristem. These explants are cultured on a medium containing more cytokinin than auxin hormone. Thus, meristem culture involves the development of an already existing shoot apical meristem and subsequently, the regeneration of adventitious root from the developed shoots.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
The transverse section of a plant shows following anatomical features:

(a) Large number of scattered vascular bundles surrounded by bundle sheath
(b) Large conspicuous parenchymatous ground tissue
(c) Vascular bundles conjoint and closed
(d) Phloem parenchyma absent

Identify the category of plant and its part:
questions.solution:
MONOCOT STEM:

a. Epidermis is uniseriate with compactly arranged barrel shaped cells covered with thick cuticle trichomes are absent.
b. Hypodermis: It is made up of a few layers of compactly arranged sclerenchyma cells. It provides mechanical support.
c. Ground tissue is the major component and is formed by an undifferentiated mass of loosely arranged parenchyma cells enclosing intercellular spaces. It is not differentiated into cortex or pith.
d. Many vascular bundles are found scattered in the ground tissue and this condition is called attactostele. From periphery to center there is a gradual decrease in the number of vascular bundles and increase in size. The vascular bundles are conjoint, collateral and closed with endarch xylem. Water filled lysigenous cavity present in association with the protoxylem. It is formed by the breakdown of inner protoxylem during earlier stages of growth. Phloem parenchyma is absent. The protophloem forms a thin layer above the functional metaphloem present towards the metaxylem. Each vascular bundle has a prominent bundle sheath made up of sclerenchyma fibres.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The chief water conducting elements of xylem in gymnosperms are
questions.solution: The tracheids are elongated, angular dead cells with hard lignified wide lumen and narrow end walls. The walls of tracheids possess different types of thickenings and the unthickened areas of its wall allow the rapid movement of water from one tracheid to another. questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Heartwood differs from sapwood in
options: being susceptible to pests and pathogens
questions.solution: As a result of continued secondary growth in subsequent years, the older part of secondary xylem or wood becomes non-functional as it loses the power of conduction. The cells of this wood are filled with resins or tannins produced by adjacent functional cells. The activities of vessels become blocked by tyloses. Due to these activities, non-functional, secondary xylem becomes hard, durable and blackish in colour, called heart-wood. Now, the function of secondary xylem (water and mineral conduction from roots) is performed by outer younger-rings of xylem, which is called sap wood.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Vascular tissues in flowering plants develop from
questions.solution:
Histogen theory for shoot apical meristem has been proposed by Hanstein (1870). It advocates that there are three distinct meristematic zones (layers) called dermatogen periblem and plerome. The dermatogen is the outermost histogen giving rise to epidermis, periblem is the middle one producing the cortex and plerome is the innermost resulting in central cylinder (ie, vascular tissue).
Cork cambium (phellogen) is the secondary lateral meristem found in outer cortical region. Its cells divide periclinally cutting off cells towards the outside (forming cork or phellem) and inside (forming secondary cortex or phelloderm).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The rupture and fractionation do not usually occur in the water column in vessel/tracheids during the ascent of sap because of
questions.solution:
The vertical conduction of water from root to aerialparts of plant is called ascent of sap. The water molecules remain joined to each other due to a force of attraction called cohesion force. This attraction is due to the presence of hydrogen bonds between them. The magnitude of this force is very high therefore, the continuous water column in the xylem cannot be broken easily due to the force of gravity or other obstructions offered by internal tissues in the upward movement of water. This adhesive property of water, ie, attraction between the water molecules and the walls of xylem ensures the continuity of water column in xylem.
Due to transpiration water evaporates to outer atmosphere through stomata. As a result leaf cells develop low water potential and water from leaf veins moves into leaf cells. The xylem vessel in turn draw water from xylem of main stem. A pressure (pull) is thus, exerted by all the leaves on the stems, which is called transpiration pull. This is strong enough to pull up the column of water to a great height.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The common bottle cork is a product of
questions.solution: The cork cambium or phellogen cells divide periclinally cutting off cells towards the outside and inside. The cells cut off towards the out side become suberized and dead. These are compactly packed in radial rows without intercellular spaces and form cork or phellem. Cork is impervious to water due to suberin and provides protection to underlying tissues. The cells cut off from cork cambium towards inside add to the cortex and are called secondary cortex cells or phelloderm cells.

Xylem vessels become dead and lose their protoplasm due to deposition of lignified secondary wall mature sieve tube elements are living cells without nucleus.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In a woody dicotyledonous tree, which of the following parts will mainly consist of primary tissues?
questions.solution: The tissues which develop from apical meristem and procambium are known as primary tissues and these constitute the primary structures of the plant body. The development of the primary tissues causes the stem to grow in length and to some extent in thickness. Stem and root in dicotyledons show secondary growth as they have development of secondary vascular tissues (i.e., secondary xylem and secondary phloem) in them. Flowers, fruits and leaves are primary tissues.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In a flowering plant, archesporium gives rise to:
options: only the wall of the sporangium
both wall and the sporogenous cells
questions.solution:
Archesporium is a cell or cell structure in a sporophyte from which spores may later develop during the alternate generation. Archesporium cell divides into the primary parietal cell which later forms the anther wall and primary sporogenous cells which form the microspore mother cell. Primary parietal wall after few more periclinal divisions forms anther wall and sporogenous cells give rise to sporogenous tissue.
Related Theory
The pollen grain grows into the male gametophyte on germination which is initiated before pollination takes place. Inside the microsporangium. Pollen mother cell (PMC) undergoes meiosis and results in four microspores which eventually mature into pollen grains.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The cells of the quiescent centre are characterised by:
options: having dense cytoplasm and prominent nuclei
having light cytoplasm and small nuclei
dividing regularly to add to the corpus
dividing regularly to add to tunica
questions.solution:
According to Quiescent Centre Theory, root apical meristem is present as the tip of main root and has a biconvex quiescent centre in its centre which is characterized by presence of inactive cells with less number of cell organelles, light cytoplasm, small nuclei and low synthesis of DNA, RNA and protein caused by low frequency of cell division, mitosis.
Related Theory
Behind the root cap is the quiescent centre. a region of inactive cells. They function to replace the meristematic cells of the root cap meristem. The quiescent centre is also important in organizing the patterns of primary growth in the root.

questions.q: What are the main components of the epidermal tissue system?
questions.solution: The epidermal tissue system forms the outer-most covering of the whole plant body and comprises epidermal cells, stomata and the epidermal appendages – the trichomes and hairs. The epidermis is the outermost layer of the primary plant body. It is made up of elongated, compactly arranged cells, which form a continuous layer. Epidermis is usually single-Layered. Epidermal cells are parenchymatous with a small amount of cytoplasm lining the cell wall and a large vacuole. The outside of the epidermis is often covered with a waxy thick layer called the cuticle which prevents the loss of water. Cuticle is absent in roots. Stomata are structures present in the epidermis of leaves. Stomata regulate the process of transpiration and gaseous exchange. Each stoma is composed of two bean-shaped cells known as guard cells which enclose stomatal pore. In grasses, the guard cells are dumb-bell shaped. The outer walls of guard cells (away from the stomatal pore) are thin and the inner walls (towards the stomatal pore) are highly thickened. The guard cells possess chloroplasts and regulate the opening and closing of stomata. Sometimes, a few epidermal cells, in the vicinity of the guard cells become specialised in their shape and size and are known as subsidiary cells. The stomatal aperture, guard cells and the surrounding subsidiary cells are together called stomatal apparatus The cells of epidermis bear a number of hairs. The root hairs are unicellular elongations of the epidermal cells and help absorb water and minerals from the soil. On the stem the epidermal hairs are called trichomes. The trichomes in the shoot system are usually multicellular. They may be branched or unbranched and soft or stiff. They may even be secretory. The trichomes help in preventing water loss due to transpiration.

Epidermal cells are parenchymatous with a small amount of cytoplasm lining the cell wall and a large vacuole. The outside of the epidermis is often covered with a waxy thick layer called the cuticle which prevents the loss of water. Cuticle is absent in roots. Stomata are structures present in the epidermis of leaves. Stomata regulate the process of transpiration and gaseous exchange. Each stoma is composed of two bean-shaped cells known as guard cells which enclose stomatal pore. In grasses, the guard cells are dumb-bell shaped. The outer walls of guard cells (away from the stomatal pore) are thin and the inner walls (towards the stomatal pore) are highly thickened. The guard cells possess chloroplasts and regulate the opening and closing of stomata. Sometimes, a few epidermal cells, in the vicinity of the guard cells become specialised in their shape and size and are known as subsidiary cells. The stomatal aperture, guard cells and the surrounding subsidiary cells are together called stomatal apparatus The cells of epidermis bear a number of hairs. The root hairs are unicellular elongations of the epidermal cells and help absorb water and minerals. On the stem the epidermal hairs are called trichomes. The trichomes in the shoot system are usually multicellular They may be branched or unbranched and soft or stiff. They may even be secretory. The trichomes help in preventing water loss due to transpiration.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What are the two main tissues that make up the vascular system?
questions.solution:
The vascular system consists of complex tissues, the phloem and the xylem. The vascular system consists of complex tissues,the phloem and the xylem.The xylem andphloem together constitute vascular bundles. In dicotyledonous stems,

cambium is present between phloem and xylem. Such vascular bundles because of the presence of cambium possess the ability to form secondary xylem and phloem tissues, and hence are called open vascular bundles. In the monocotyledons, the vascular bundles have no cambium present in them. Hence, since they do not form secondary tissues they are referred to as closed. When xylem and phloem within a vascular bundle are arranged in an alternate manner along the different radii, the arrangement is called radial such as in roots. In conjoint type of vascular bundles, the xylem and phloem are jointly situated along the same radius of vascular bundles. Such vascular bundles are common in stems and leaves. The conjoint vascular bundles usually have the phloem located only on the outer side of xylem.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the outermost layer of a dicot root ?
questions.solution: : The outermost layer is epiblema. Many of the cells of epiblema protrude in the form of unicellular root hairs. The cortex consists of several layers of thin-walled parenchyma cells with intercellular spaces. The innermost layer of the cortex is called endodermis. It comprises a single layer of barrel-shaped cells without any intercellular spaces. The tangential as well as radial walls of the endodermal cells have a deposition of water-impermeable, waxy material suberin in the form of casparian strips. Next to endodermis lies a few layers of thick-walled parenchyomatous cells referred to as pericycle. Initiation of lateral roots and vascular cambium during the secondary growth takes place in these cells. The pith is small or inconspicuous.The parenchymatous cells which lie between the xylem and the phloem are called conjuctive tissue. There are usually two to four xylem and phloem patches. Later, a cambium ring develops between the xylem and phloem. All tissues on the innerside of the endodermis such as pericycle, vascular bundles and pith constitute the stele.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the function of the hypodermis in a young dicotyledonous stem?
questions.solution: The transverse section of a typical young dicotyledonous stem shows that the epidermis is the outermost protective layer of the stem Covered with a thin layer of cuticle, it may bear trichomes and a few stomata. The cells arranged in multiple layers between epidermis and pericycle constitute the cortex. It consists of three sub-zones. The outer hypodermis, consists of a few layers of collenchymatous cells just below the epidermis, which provide mechanical strength to the young stem. Cortical layers below hypodermis consist of rounded thin walled parenchymatous cells with conspicuous intercellular spaces. The innermost layer of the cortex is called the endodermis. The cells of the endodermis are rich in starch grains and the layer is also referred to as the starch sheath. Pericycle is present on the inner side of the endodermis and above the phloem in the form of semi-lunar patches of sclerenchyma. In between the vascular bundles there are a few layers of radially placed parenchymatous cells, which constitute medullary rays. A large number of vascular bundles are arranged in a ring ; the ‘ring’ arrangement of vascular bundles is a characteristic of dicot stem. Each vascular bundle is conjoint, open, and with endarch protoxylem. A large number of rounded, parenchymatous cells with large intercellularspaces which occupy the central portion of the stem constitute the pith.

questions.q: What is the outermost layer of the monocot stem?
questions.solution: . The monocot stem has a sclerenchymatous hypodermis, a large number of scattered vascular bundles, each surrounded by a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath, and a large, conspicuous parenchymatous ground tissue. Vascular bundles are conjoint and closed. Peripheral vascular bundles are generally smaller than the centrally located ones. The phloem parenchyma is absent, and water-containing cavities are present within the vascular bundles.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the outermost protective layer of a leaf?
questions.solution: The vertical section of a dorsiventral leaf through the lamina shows three main parts, namely, epidermis, mesophyll and vascular system. The epidermis which covers both the upper surface (adaxial epidermis) and lower surface (abaxial epidermis) of the leaf has a conspicuous cuticle. The abaxial epidermis generally bears more stomata than the adaxial epidermis. The latter may even lack stomata. The tissue between the upper and the lower epidermis is called the mesophyll. Mesophyll, which possesses chloroplasts and carry out photosynthesis, is made up of parenchyma. It has two types of cells – the palisade parenchyma and the spongy parenchyma. The adaxially placed palisade parenchyma is made up of elongated cells, which are arranged vertically and parallel to each other. The oval or round and loosely arranged spongy parenchyma is situated below the palisade cells and extends to the lower epidermis. There are numerous large spaces and air cavities between these cells. Vascular system includes vascular bundles, which can be seen in the veins and the midrib. The size of the vascular bundles are dependent on the size of the veins. The veins vary in thickness in the reticulate venation of the dicot leaves. The vascular bundles are surrounded by a layer of thick walled bundle sheath cells. and find the position of xylem in the vascular bundle.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the role of bulliform cells in grass leaves?
options: They help in prevention of water loss and leaf curling
They are responsible for the parallel venation in monocot leaves
They are responsible for the reticulate venation in dicot leaves
questions.solution: The anatomy of isobilateral leaf is similar to that of the dorsiventral leaf in many ways. It shows the following characteristic differences. In an isobilateral leaf, the stomata are present on both the surfaces of the epidermis; and the mesophyll is not differentiated into palisade and spongy parenchyma . In grasses, certain adaxial epidermal cells along the veins modify themselves into large, empty, colourless cells. These are called bulliform cells. When the bulliform cells in the leaves have absorbed water and are turgid, the leaf surface is exposed. When they are flaccid due to water stress, they make the leaves curl inwards to minimise water loss. The parallel venation in monocot leaves is reflected in the near similar sizes of vascular bundles (except in main veins) as seen in vertical sections of the leaves.

questions.q: The given structure is found in which of the following plants?

The guard cells possess chloroplasts and regulate the opening and closing of stomata.

questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding the anatomy of a dicotyledonous root:

Statement I: The innermost layer of the cortex is the endodermis.
Statement II: Root hairs are unicellular elongations of the epiblema.
Statement III: Lateral roots originate exogenously from the epiblema.
Statement IV: Vascular cambium in dicot roots is partly primary and partly secondary in origin.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement I is correct: The cortex consists of several layers of thin-walled parenchyma cells, and its innermost layer is the endodermis.

Statement II is correct: The outermost layer of the root is the epiblema. Many of its cells protrude in the form of unicellular root hairs.

Statement III is incorrect: Lateral roots have an endogenous origin as they arise from the pericycle, which is located deep within the root.

Statement IV is incorrect: In dicot roots, the vascular cambium is completely secondary in origin. It originates from the tissue located just below the phloem bundles and a portion of pericycle tissue above the protoxylem.

Therefore, exactly two statements (I and II) are correct.

Answer: Only two

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: During conditions of water stress, what is the physical state of the bulliform cells in grass leaves and its consequent effect on the leaf lamina?
options: They become flaccid and make the leaves curl inwards.
They become turgid and make the leaves curl inwards.
They become flaccid and expose the leaf surface.
They become turgid and expose the leaf surface.
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, in grasses, certain adaxial epidermal cells along the veins modify themselves into large, empty, colourless cells called bulliform cells.

When the bulliform cells in the leaves have absorbed water and are turgid, the leaf surface is exposed. When they are flaccid due to water stress, they make the leaves curl inwards to minimise water loss.

Answer: They become flaccid and make the leaves curl inwards.

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In the vertical section of an isobilateral leaf, the vascular bundles are generally seen to be of near similar sizes.
Reason (R): The near similar sizes of vascular bundles in isobilateral leaves is due to the presence of reticulate venation.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true because in isobilateral (monocotyledonous) leaves, the vascular bundles are generally of near similar sizes (except in main veins) as seen in vertical sections.

Reason (R) is false because isobilateral leaves typically possess parallel venation, not reticulate venation. It is this parallel venation that is reflected in the near similar sizes of the vascular bundles. Reticulate venation is a characteristic of dicotyledonous (dorsiventral) leaves, where the vascular bundles vary greatly in size depending on the size of the veins.

Answer: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

Thus, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) correctly explains why the innermost layer of the cortex is called the starch sheath.

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
A student observes a transverse section of a plant part under a microscope and notes the following anatomical features:

(a) Vascular bundles are radial with exarch protoxylem.
(b) Xylem bundles are more than six in number (polyarch condition).
(c) A large and well-developed pith is present in the center.

Identify the category of the plant and its part:
questions.solution:
The presence of radial vascular bundles and an exarch condition of protoxylem are characteristic features of roots, distinguishing them from stems (which have conjoint bundles and endarch protoxylem).

Among roots, the presence of more than six xylem bundles (polyarch condition) and a large, well-developed pith are specific diagnostic features of a monocotyledonous root. In contrast, a dicotyledonous root typically has fewer xylem patches (usually two to four, or diarch to tetrarch) and a small, inconspicuous pith.

Answer: Monocotyledonous root

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match List I with List II regarding the characteristics of vascular bundles.

List I (Plant Organ)List II (Vascular Bundle Features)
A. Dicotyledonous rootI. Radial vascular bundles, usually two to four xylem patches
B. Monocotyledonous rootII. Radial vascular bundles, polyarch xylem
C. Dicotyledonous stemIII. Conjoint and open vascular bundles arranged in a ring
D. Monocotyledonous stemIV. Conjoint and closed vascular bundles scattered in ground tissue

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
In roots, vascular bundles are radial (xylem and phloem are arranged alternately on different radii). Dicotyledonous roots typically have two to four (diarch to tetrarch) xylem patches, whereas monocotyledonous roots have more than six (polyarch) xylem bundles.

In stems, vascular bundles are conjoint (xylem and phloem are situated on the same radius). Dicotyledonous stems possess open vascular bundles (cambium is present) that are arranged in a characteristic ring. Monocotyledonous stems have closed vascular bundles (cambium is absent) that are scattered throughout the ground tissue.

Answer: A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding the anatomy of a dorsiventral leaf:

(A) The abaxial epidermis generally bears more stomata than the adaxial epidermis.
(B) The spongy parenchyma is situated adaxially and consists of loosely arranged cells.
(C) The size of vascular bundles is dependent on the size of the veins.
(D) The veins vary in thickness in the reticulate venation of dicot leaves.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is correct. In a dorsiventral (dicotyledonous) leaf, the lower (abaxial) surface bears more stomata than the upper surface to prevent excessive water loss.

Statement (B) is incorrect. The spongy parenchyma is situated abaxially (below the palisade cells and extending to the lower epidermis), while the palisade parenchyma is placed adaxially.

Statement (C) is correct. The vascular system includes vascular bundles seen in the veins and midrib, and their size is dependent on the size of the veins.

Statement (D) is correct. Dicot leaves exhibit reticulate venation, where the veins vary in thickness.

Therefore, exactly three statements ((A), (C), and (D)) are correct.

Answer: Three

Read the following statements regarding the vascular cambium in a dicot stem:

(A) Intrafascicular cambium is present between primary xylem and primary phloem.
(B) Interfascicular cambium is formed by the dedifferentiation of endodermal cells.
(C) The continuous cambial ring is partly primary and partly secondary in origin.
(D) Interfascicular cambium is an example of a primary meristem.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is correct as the cambium present inside the vascular bundle, between primary xylem and primary phloem, is the intrafascicular cambium.

Statement (B) is incorrect because interfascicular cambium is formed by the dedifferentiation of medullary ray cells, not endodermal cells.

Statement (C) is correct because the continuous cambial ring is formed by both intrafascicular cambium (which is primary in origin) and interfascicular cambium (which is secondary in origin).

Statement (D) is incorrect because interfascicular cambium appears later in the life of the plant and is formed by dedifferentiation of permanent tissues, making it a secondary meristem.

Therefore, exactly two statements are correct.

Answer: Two

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In a dorsiventral leaf, the adaxial epidermis generally bears fewer stomata than the abaxial epidermis, or may even lack stomata.

Reason (R): The mesophyll of a dorsiventral leaf is differentiated into adaxially placed palisade parenchyma and abaxially placed spongy parenchyma.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true. In a dorsiventral (dicotyledonous) leaf, the upper (adaxial) epidermis is directly exposed to sunlight. To minimize water loss through transpiration, it generally bears fewer stomata than the lower (abaxial) epidermis, and may even lack them entirely.

Reason (R) is also true. The mesophyll in dicot leaves is differentiated into an upper (adaxial) palisade parenchyma made of elongated cells and a lower (abaxial) spongy parenchyma made of loosely arranged cells.

However, Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A). The differentiation of the mesophyll into palisade and spongy layers does not cause the differential distribution of stomata on the epidermis; both are independent anatomical adaptations of a dorsiventral leaf.

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

questions.q: Which of the following combinations of epidermal features correctly describes an isobilateral leaf?
options: Stomata are present only on the lower surface and bulliform cells are on the adaxial epidermis.
Stomata are present on both the surfaces and bulliform cells are on the adaxial epidermis.
Stomata are present on both the surfaces and bulliform cells are on the abaxial epidermis.
Stomata are present only on the upper surface and bulliform cells are absent.
questions.solution:
In an isobilateral (monocotyledonous) leaf, the stomata are present on both the surfaces of the epidermis. This is in contrast to dorsiventral (dicotyledonous) leaves, where stomata are generally more numerous on the lower surface.

Additionally, in grasses, certain adaxial epidermal cells along the veins modify themselves into large, empty, colourless cells known as bulliform cells. Therefore, an isobilateral leaf is characterised by stomata on both surfaces and the presence of bulliform cells on the adaxial epidermis.

Answer: Stomata are present on both the surfaces and bulliform cells are on the adaxial epidermis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Consider the following plant tissues:
(i) Shoot apical meristem
(ii) Intrafascicular cambium
(iii) Interfascicular cambium
(iv) Cork cambium
(v) Intercalary meristem

Which of the above are strictly secondary meristems formed by the process of dedifferentiation?
questions.solution:
Shoot apical meristem and intercalary meristem are primary meristems as they appear early in the life of a plant and contribute to the primary plant body.

Intrafascicular cambium (fascicular vascular cambium) is present between primary xylem and primary phloem in dicot stems from the beginning, making it primary in origin, even though it is a lateral meristem.

Interfascicular cambium is formed later when fully differentiated medullary ray cells regain the capacity to divide (dedifferentiation).

Cork cambium (phellogen) is also formed by the dedifferentiation of permanent cells in the cortex region during secondary growth.

Thus, only interfascicular cambium and cork cambium are strictly secondary meristems formed by dedifferentiation.

Answer: (iii) and (iv) only

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Secondary xylem and secondary phloem are considered redifferentiated tissues.
Reason (R): They are formed by the division of primary meristems and subsequently lose their capacity to divide to perform specific functions.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct: Secondary xylem and secondary phloem are formed by the division of vascular cambium (a dedifferentiated tissue). The newly formed cells lose their capacity to divide and mature to perform specific functions. This phenomenon is termed redifferentiation.

Reason (R) is incorrect: Secondary xylem and secondary phloem are formed by the division of secondary meristems (vascular cambium), not primary meristems. Primary meristems form primary permanent tissues through differentiation.

Answer: Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.

Assertion (A): In stems, the primary xylem is endarch, whereas in roots, the primary xylem is exarch.

Reason (R): In stems, protoxylem lies towards the centre and metaxylem towards the periphery; in roots, protoxylem lies towards the periphery and metaxylem towards the centre.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
questions.solution:
The Assertion correctly states the condition of primary xylem in stems (endarch) and roots (exarch).

The Reason correctly defines these terms based on the relative positions of protoxylem (first formed primary xylem) and metaxylem (later formed primary xylem). In stems, the protoxylem lies towards the centre (pith) and the metaxylem lies towards the periphery, which is the exact definition of the endarch condition. In roots, the protoxylem lies towards the periphery and the metaxylem lies towards the centre, which defines the exarch condition.

Since the Reason provides the exact anatomical definitions that justify the terminology used in the Assertion, both statements are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.q:
Read the following description of a plant tissue:

"It consists of dead cells that are spherical, oval or cylindrical in shape, possessing highly thickened walls and very narrow cavities. They are commonly found in the fruit walls of nuts and the pulp of fruits like pear and sapota."

Identify the specific tissue described above.
questions.solution:
The description given exactly matches sclereids, which are a type of sclerenchyma tissue. According to NCERT, sclereids are spherical, oval or cylindrical, highly thickened dead cells with very narrow cavities (lumen). They are commonly found in the fruit walls of nuts; pulp of fruits like guava, pear and sapota; seed coats of legumes and leaves of tea.

Sclerenchyma fibres are thick-walled, elongated and pointed cells. Vessels are cylindrical tube-like structures made of many cells (vessel members) with lignified walls and a large central cavity, involved in water transport. Collenchyma consists of living cells with localized wall thickenings and no narrow cavities.

Answer: Sclereids

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Interfascicular cambium is considered a primary lateral meristem.
Reason (R): It is formed later in the life of the plant by the dedifferentiation of permanent cells of medullary rays.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is incorrect because interfascicular cambium is a secondary lateral meristem, not a primary one. Primary meristems appear early in the life of a plant (e.g., apical meristems, intrafascicular cambium).

Reason (R) is correct. Interfascicular cambium originates later in the plant's life during secondary growth. It is formed when the fully differentiated, permanent parenchymatous cells of the medullary rays regain the capacity to divide (dedifferentiation). Because of this later origin from permanent tissues, it is classified as a secondary meristem.

Answer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Sclerenchyma cells are dead and usually lack protoplasts at maturity.
Reason (R): They possess highly thickened walls with abundant lignin deposition and very narrow lumens.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true because sclerenchyma cells are typically dead at maturity and do not contain living protoplasts.

Reason (R) is true and correctly explains the Assertion. The heavy deposition of impermeable lignin on the cell walls makes them highly thickened and severely reduces the lumen size. This extensive lignification prevents the exchange of water and nutrients, inevitably leading to the death of the protoplast as the cell matures.

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.

questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding the anatomy of a monocotyledonous stem:

(i) A sclerenchymatous bundle sheath surrounds each vascular bundle.
(ii) Phloem parenchyma is present.
(iii) Water-containing cavities are present within the vascular bundles.
(iv) Vascular bundles are arranged in a ring.
(v) Peripheral vascular bundles are generally smaller than the centrally located ones.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Let us evaluate each statement based on the anatomy of a monocot stem:

(i) Correct. Each vascular bundle in a monocot stem is surrounded by a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath.
(ii) Incorrect. Phloem parenchyma is absent in monocot stems.
(iii) Correct. Water-containing cavities are a characteristic feature present within the vascular bundles of monocot stems.
(iv) Incorrect. The vascular bundles are scattered in the ground tissue, not arranged in a ring (which is a feature of dicot stems).
(v) Correct. The peripheral vascular bundles are generally smaller than the centrally located ones.

Thus, exactly three statements ((i), (iii), and (v)) are correct.

Answer: Three

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding leaf anatomy:

Statement A: In grasses, certain adaxial epidermal cells modify into large, empty, colourless cells.
Statement B: When bulliform cells are turgid, they make the leaf curl inwards.
Statement C: Bulliform cells are absent in dorsiventral leaves.
Statement D: In an isobilateral leaf, the vascular bundles are nearly similar in size, except in main veins.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement A is correct as in grasses, certain adaxial epidermal cells along the veins modify themselves into large, empty, colourless cells called bulliform cells.

Statement B is incorrect because when bulliform cells are turgid, the leaf surface is exposed. They make the leaves curl inwards to minimise water loss only when they become flaccid due to water stress.

Statement C is correct as bulliform cells are a characteristic feature of isobilateral (monocot) leaves, such as grasses, and are absent in dorsiventral (dicot) leaves.

Statement D is correct because in monocot (isobilateral) leaves, parallel venation is present, which is reflected in the near similar sizes of vascular bundles (except in main veins).

Thus, three statements (A, C, and D) are correct.

Answer: Three

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
A student observes the transverse section of a leaf under a microscope and notes the following features:
(a) The mesophyll is not differentiated into palisade and spongy parenchyma.
(b) The upper epidermis possesses some large, empty, and colourless cells along the veins.

Identify the likely group of plants to which this leaf belongs, and the primary function of the specialised cells mentioned in feature (b).
options: Monocotyledonous plant; minimising water loss by leaf curling
Dicotyledonous plant; providing large spaces for storage of sugars
Dicotyledonous plant; minimising water loss by leaf curling
questions.solution:
The presence of an undifferentiated mesophyll (no distinct palisade and spongy parenchyma) is a characteristic feature of an isobilateral leaf, which is typically found in monocotyledonous plants.

The large, empty, and colourless cells on the upper (adaxial) epidermis are bulliform cells. In grasses (monocots), these cells help in minimising water loss during water stress by becoming flaccid, which causes the leaves to curl inwards.

Therefore, the leaf belongs to a monocotyledonous plant, and the specialised cells function to minimise water loss by leaf curling. Bundle sheath cells, not bulliform cells, are involved in C4 photosynthesis.

Answer: Monocotyledonous plant; minimising water loss by leaf curling

(A) Simple tissues are made of only one type of cells.
(B) Vascular tissues in plants are examples of complex tissues.
(C) Cells of meristematic tissues lack the capacity to divide.
(D) Sclereids are living cells with thin cellulosic cell walls.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is correct as simple tissues consist of structurally and functionally similar cells.

Statement (B) is correct because vascular tissues (xylem and phloem) are complex tissues made of different types of cells working together as a unit.

Statement (C) is incorrect because meristematic tissues are characterised by their active cell division capacity.

Statement (D) is incorrect because sclereids are a type of sclerenchyma, which are dead cells with highly thickened, lignified walls and very narrow cavities (lumens).

Therefore, exactly two statements are correct.

Answer: Only two

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: During secondary growth in a dicot stem, the interfascicular cambium is formed by the dedifferentiation of which of the following permanent tissues?
questions.solution:
In dicot stems, the cells of the medullary rays adjoining the intrafascicular cambium become meristematic through the process of dedifferentiation. This newly formed meristematic tissue is called the interfascicular cambium.

The intrafascicular cambium is already present as a primary meristem between the primary xylem and primary phloem. The pericycle is involved in forming lateral roots and cork cambium in roots, but not the interfascicular cambium in stems. The endodermis does not dedifferentiate to form the vascular cambium.

Answer: Cells of medullary rays
questions.question: During secondary growth in a dicot stem, the interfascicular cambium is formed by the dedifferentiation of which of the following permanent tissues?
questions.explanation:
In dicot stems, the cells of the medullary rays adjoining the intrafascicular cambium become meristematic through the process of dedifferentiation. This newly formed meristematic tissue is called the interfascicular cambium.

The intrafascicular cambium is already present as a primary meristem between the primary xylem and primary phloem. The pericycle is involved in forming lateral roots and cork cambium in roots, but not the interfascicular cambium in stems. The endodermis does not dedifferentiate to form the vascular cambium.

Answer: Cells of medullary rays

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following pairs of tissue descriptions and their corresponding examples is incorrectly matched?
options: Tissue having all cells similar in structure and function : Phloem in angiosperms
Tissue with active cell division : Intercalary meristem in grasses
Dead cells with highly thickened walls and narrow lumen : Sclereids in pulp of guava
Tissue having all cells similar in structure and function : Parenchyma in cortex
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, simple tissues are made of only one type of cells (all cells similar in structure and function), such as parenchyma, collenchyma, and sclerenchyma. Complex tissues are made of more than one type of cells and work together as a unit. Phloem is a complex tissue, not a simple tissue. In angiosperms, phloem is composed of four different types of cells: sieve tube elements, companion cells, phloem parenchyma, and phloem fibres.

Intercalary meristem in grasses is a meristematic tissue capable of active cell division. Parenchyma in the cortex is a simple tissue. Sclereids in the pulp of guava are dead cells with highly thickened walls and narrow cavities.

Answer: Tissue having all cells similar in structure and function : Phloem in angiosperms
questions.question: Which of the following pairs of tissue descriptions and their corresponding examples is incorrectly matched?
questions.explanation:

Intercalary meristem in grasses is a meristematic tissue capable of active cell division. Parenchyma in the cortex is a simple tissue. Sclereids in the pulp of guava are dead cells with highly thickened walls and narrow cavities.

Answer: Tissue having all cells similar in structure and function : Phloem in angiosperms

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) Intercalary meristem(I) Present in the axils of leaves
(B) Cork cambium(II) Occurs between mature tissues
(C) Axillary bud(III) Lateral meristem responsible for secondary growth
(D) Apical meristem(IV) Produces primary tissues at root/shoot tips

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Intercalary meristems occur between mature tissues, such as at the base of internodes in grasses.

Cork cambium is a cylindrical lateral meristem that appears later in the life of a plant and is responsible for secondary growth (producing cork and secondary cortex).

Axillary buds are formed by cells left behind from the shoot apical meristem and are present in the axils of leaves.

Apical meristems occur at the tips of roots and shoots and produce primary tissues.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV).

Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV)

questions.q: During secondary growth in dicot stems, the formation of phelloderm from phellogen is an example of which of the following developmental processes?
questions.solution:
Phellogen (cork cambium) is a secondary meristem formed by the process of dedifferentiation. When the cells of phellogen divide and the newly formed cells mature to form phelloderm (secondary cortex), they lose their capacity to divide.

According to NCERT, the process by which the derivatives of a dedifferentiated tissue lose their ability to divide and mature to perform specific functions is called redifferentiation.

Dedifferentiation is incorrect because it refers to the formation of the phellogen itself, not its products. Differentiation applies to primary tissues, and plasticity refers to different pathways in response to environment or phases of life.

Answer: Redifferentiation

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the characteristics of vascular bundles in three unidentified plant parts (X, Y, and Z):

Part X: Radial arrangement, exarch protoxylem, cambium absent.
Part Y: Conjoint arrangement, endarch protoxylem, cambium present.
Part Z: Conjoint arrangement, endarch protoxylem, cambium absent.

Identify the correct sequence of plant parts corresponding to X, Y, and Z.
options: X - Root, Y - Dicot stem, Z - Monocot stem
X - Dicot stem, Y - Root, Z - Monocot stem
X - Root, Y - Monocot stem, Z - Dicot stem
X - Root, Y - Dicot root, Z - Monocot stem
questions.solution:
Part X has a radial arrangement of vascular bundles (xylem and phloem arranged alternately along different radii) and exarch protoxylem (protoxylem lies towards the periphery). These are characteristic features of roots. The primary bundles in roots also lack cambium.

Part Y has conjoint vascular bundles (xylem and phloem situated at the same radius) with endarch protoxylem (protoxylem lies towards the centre). These features indicate a stem. The presence of cambium between xylem and phloem makes it an 'open' vascular bundle, which is a characteristic of dicotyledonous stems.

Part Z also has conjoint vascular bundles and endarch protoxylem, indicating it is a stem. However, cambium is absent, making it a 'closed' vascular bundle. This is a characteristic feature of monocotyledonous stems.

Thus, the correct sequence is X - Root, Y - Dicot stem, Z - Monocot stem.

Answer: X - Root, Y - Dicot stem, Z - Monocot stem

Therefore, the correct matching is (A) - (III), (B) - (I), (C) - (II).

Answer: (A) - (III), (B) - (I), (C) - (II)

Read the following statements regarding plant growth and development:

Statement A: Plant growth is open, but differentiation in plants is closed.
Statement B: The formation of cork from cork cambium is an example of redifferentiation.
Statement C: Tracheary elements develop highly lignified cell walls during dedifferentiation.
Statement D: Living differentiated cells can regain the capacity to divide under certain conditions.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement A is incorrect: Like growth, differentiation in plants is also open, because cells or tissues arising out of the same meristem can have different structures at maturity.

Statement B is correct: Cork is formed when cells cut off by the cork cambium (a secondary meristem) lose their capacity to divide and mature. This process is called redifferentiation.

Statement C is incorrect: The development of highly lignified cell walls and loss of protoplasm to form tracheary elements are events that occur during differentiation (maturation), not dedifferentiation.

Statement D is correct: The phenomenon where living differentiated cells regain the capacity to divide under certain conditions is termed dedifferentiation.

Therefore, exactly two statements (B and D) are correct.

Answer: Two

Monocotyledonous roots typically show a polyarch condition (usually more than six xylem bundles), whereas dicotyledonous roots usually have two to four (diarch to tetrarch) xylem patches.

The pith is small or inconspicuous in dicotyledonous roots, whereas it is large and well-developed in monocotyledonous roots.

Answer: (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In a young dicot stem, the intrafascicular cambium is located :
options: Between primary xylem and primary phloem
Between secondary xylem and secondary phloem
questions.solution:
In a young dicot stem, the vascular bundles are open, meaning they contain a strip of cambium within them. This cambium, present inherently inside the vascular bundle between the primary xylem and primary phloem, is called the intrafascicular (or fascicular) cambium.

The cambium that forms between two adjacent vascular bundles is the interfascicular cambium. Secondary xylem and secondary phloem are tissues produced later by the activity of the continuous cambial ring.

Answer: Between primary xylem and primary phloem

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding the transverse section of a typical dicotyledonous stem?
options: The innermost layer of the cortex is called the endodermis, and its cells are rich in starch grains.
The pericycle is present on the inner side of the endodermis and above the phloem in the form of semi-lunar patches of sclerenchyma.
The vascular bundles are conjoint, open, and arranged in a characteristic ring.
The ground tissue is an undifferentiated mass of loosely arranged parenchyma cells.
questions.solution:
In a typical dicotyledonous stem, the ground tissue is well-differentiated into distinct regions: the cortex (hypodermis, general cortex, and endodermis), pericycle, medullary rays, and pith. The endodermis is often referred to as the starch sheath, and the pericycle occurs as semi-lunar patches of sclerenchyma above the phloem. The vascular bundles are conjoint, open, and arranged in a ring.

An undifferentiated ground tissue is a characteristic feature of a monocotyledonous stem, not a dicotyledonous stem. Therefore, the statement describing an undifferentiated ground tissue is incorrect for a dicot stem.

Answer: The ground tissue is an undifferentiated mass of loosely arranged parenchyma cells.

options: Cambium present between primary xylem and primary phloem
Vascular bundles surrounded by a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath
questions.solution:
The presence of radial vascular bundles with exarch protoxylem is a characteristic feature of roots. The tetrarch condition (four xylem patches) specifically identifies the plant axis as a dicotyledonous root, since monocotyledonous roots typically have a polyarch condition (more than six xylem bundles).

In a dicotyledonous root, the pith is small or inconspicuous.

A large and well-developed pith is found in monocotyledonous roots. Cambium present between primary xylem and primary phloem is a feature of conjoint open vascular bundles in dicotyledonous stems. Vascular bundles surrounded by a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath are characteristic of monocotyledonous stems.

Answer: A small or inconspicuous pith

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In a dicotyledonous root, the cells of the pericycle are responsible for the initiation of:
options: lateral branches of stem and cork cambium
questions.solution:
In a dicotyledonous root, the pericycle is the layer of cells located just inside the endodermis. According to NCERT, the initiation of lateral roots and the vascular cambium during secondary growth takes place in these pericycle cells.

Root hairs arise exogenously from the outermost layer (epiblema). Casparian strips are a characteristic feature of the endodermis, not the pericycle. Lateral branches of stems have an exogenous origin, unlike the endogenous origin of lateral roots from the pericycle.

Answer: lateral roots and vascular cambium

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Leaves of grasses curl inwards during severe water stress.
Reason (R): During water stress, bulliform cells present on the adaxial epidermis become highly turgid, which makes the leaves curl inwards.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct because in grasses, leaves curl inwards during severe water stress to minimise water loss by reducing the exposed surface area.

Reason (R) is incorrect because the inward curling of leaves is caused when the bulliform cells become flaccid due to water stress. When these cells absorb water and become turgid, the leaf surface is exposed, not curled.

Answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements carefully:
(A) Intercalary meristems regenerate parts removed by grazing herbivores in grasses.
(B) Cells 'left behind' from the shoot apical meristem constitute the axillary bud.
(C) All lateral meristems are strictly secondary in origin.
(D) Fascicular vascular cambium is an example of a lateral meristem.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is correct as intercalary meristems occur in grasses and regenerate parts removed by grazing herbivores.

Statement (B) is correct because during the formation of leaves and elongation of stem, some cells 'left behind' from the shoot apical meristem constitute the axillary bud.

Statement (C) is incorrect because not all lateral meristems are secondary in origin. Fascicular vascular cambium (intrafascicular cambium) is a lateral meristem but is primary in origin, as it exists from the beginning between primary xylem and primary phloem.

Statement (D) is correct as fascicular vascular cambium, interfascicular cambium, and cork cambium are examples of lateral meristems.

Therefore, exactly three statements are correct.

Answer: Three

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements carefully:
(A) Conjunctive tissue is the parenchymatous tissue present between xylem and phloem in roots.
(B) The endodermis of a dicot stem is rich in starch grains and is referred to as the starch sheath.
(C) Casparian strips are water-permeable depositions of lignin found in the pericycle.
(D) Subsidiary cells are specialised mesophyll cells found in the leaves of all angiosperms.

How many of the given statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is correct as conjunctive tissue is the parenchymatous tissue lying between the xylem and the phloem in roots.

Statement (B) is correct because the innermost layer of the cortex in a dicot stem is the endodermis, and its cells are rich in starch grains, hence it is called the starch sheath.

Statement (C) is incorrect because Casparian strips are water-impermeable, waxy depositions of suberin (not lignin) found in the endodermis (not pericycle) of roots.

Statement (D) is incorrect because subsidiary cells are specialised epidermal cells (not mesophyll cells) present in the vicinity of guard cells.

Therefore, exactly two statements are correct.

Answer: Only two

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : Annual rings are used to calculate the age of tree.
Reason : Secondary growth is not found in bamboo.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: Each year the tree forms new cells (secondary growth) arranged in concentric circles called annual rings. These rings show amount of wood produced during one growing season. By counting the annual rings, the age of a tree can be determined. This phenomenon is called dendrochronology. Only plants showing secondary growth show annual rings. Bamboo is a monocot and hence secondary growth is absent in bamboo.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: As secondary growth proceeds, in a dicot stem, the thickness of
options: both sapwood and heartwood remains the same.
questions.solution: In a woody stem, due to secondary growth, secondary xylem constitutes the bulk of the stem and is commonly called wood. The secondary xylem consists of vessels, tracheids, wood parenchyma and wood fibres. Width of secondary xylem increases continuously with the age of the plant. In older stems, the wood (or secondary xylem) gets differentiated into two zones - the outer light coloured younger sapwood and the inner darker older heartwood. The xylem vessels and tracheids of heartwood become non-functional because they get filled with resins, tannins, gums etc. produced by adjacent living parenchymatous cells and due to tyloses. Changes in the nature of sapwood occur with the death of parenchyma cells and with the completion of these changes, heartwood is formed. Thus, the conversion of sapwood into heartwood is a progressive phenomenon which continues throughout the life of the plant. Initially, both sapwood and heartwood increase in size but as a tree reaches a certain age, amount of heartwood increases continuously and the amount of sapwood remains almost constant.

Assertion : No secondary growth takes place in monocots.

If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: Secondary growth is the growth in thickness due to the formation of secondary tissues by lateral meristems. With the exception of some annuals, most of the dicots and gymnosperms show secondary growth in their stems and roots. It takes place by the production of two types of secondary tissues : secondary vascular tissues and periderm. These tissues are formed by meristems, vascular cambium and cork cambium respectively. Secondary growth does not occur in monocots because monocots do not possess vascular cambium in between the vascular bundles.

questions.subject: Botany

options: Spring wood – light colour, high density

Autumn wood – light colour, high density
Autumn wood – dark colour, high density
questions.solution: The yearly growth of secondary xylem is distinct in the area which experiences two seasons, one favourable (spring or rainy season) and the other unfavourable (autumn, winter and dry summer). The wood formed in a single year consists of two types of wood, spring wood and autumn wood. The spring or early wood is much wider than the autumn or late wood. It is lighter in colour and of lower density. Spring wood consists of larger and wider xylem elements. The autumn or late wood is dark coloured and of higher density. It contains compactly arranged smaller and narrower elements which have comparatively thicker walls. In autumn wood, tracheids and fibres are more abundant than those found in the spring wood.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Why are vascular bundles closed in monocots?
options: Xylem and phloem occur in separate bundles.
Vascular cambium is present between xylem and phloem.
questions.solution: The vascular system consists of complex tissues, the phloem and the xylem. The xylem and phloem together constitute vascular bundles. In dicotyledonous stems, cambium is present between phloem and xylem. Such vascular bundles because of the presence of cambium possess the ability to form secondary xylem and phloem tissues, and hence are called open vascular bundles. In the monocotyledons, the vascular bundles have no cambium present in them. Hence, since they do not form secondary tissues so they are referred to as closed.

questions.solution: Cork consists of dead and compactly arranged rectangular cells that possess suberised cell walls. The cork cells contain tannins. Hence, they appear brown or dark brown in colour. The cork cells of some plants are filled with air. Cork prevents the loss of water by evaporation. It also protects the interior against entry of harmful micro-organisms, mechanical injury and extremes of temperature. Cork is light, compressible, nonreactive and sufficiently resistant to fire. It is used as stopper for bottles, shock absorption and insulation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Bark refers to
questions.solution: Bark is a loose term and is used to define all the tissues outside vascular cambium. It is differentiated into outer bark or rhytidome (consisting of dead cells) and inner bark (of living cells, i.e., periderm, cortex, pericycle and secondary phloem). The outer layers of the bark are being constantly peeled off on account of the formation of new secondary vascular tissues in the interior. Bark is insect repellent, decay proof, fire-proof and acts as a heat screen.

Assertion : In woody stems, the amount of heart wood continues to increase year after year.
Reason : The cambial activity continues uninterrupted.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false

questions.solution: Heartwood formation occurs spontaneously because it is a genetically programmed process. As a result of continued secondary growth for several years, the older parts of the stem and its old branches have a part of its secondary xylem rendered non - functional. Such a modified and non - functional secondary xylem is called the heart wood or duramen, the functional outer younger rings of secondary xylem constitute the sap wood or alburnum. With the passage of time and addition of new outer rings of secondary xylem due to cambial activity more rings of the sap wood are changed into heart wood. This leads to the increase in the thickness of heart wood, whereas the sap wood remains of about the same thickness.

questions.solution: Sieve elements are a component of phloem tissue and are responsible for conduction of food in plants. A sieve tube element has peripheral layer of cytoplasm without any nucleus. The central part is occupied by a network of canals which contain fibrils of $p$-protein. The protein is vibratite and is believed to actively participate in the transport of nutrients. One general property of its ability to form a gel and it functions as a puncture repair substance forming a plug at any site of damage in sieve element, thus preventing loss of food materials being translocated by the phloem. Thus it is believed to have sealing function on wounding.

questions.q:
Assertion : In angiosperms the conduction of water is more efficient because their xylem has vessels.
Reason : Conduction of water by vessel elements is an active process with energy supplied by xylem parenchyma rich in mitochondria.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of the assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion
If assertion is true, but reason is false
Both assertion and reason are false statements.
questions.solution: Xylem is the main conducting tissue in plants. It consists of 4 different components - tracheids, trachea or vessels, xylem fibre and xylem parenchyma. Tracheids are elongated cells with tapering end. They are generally present in ferns and gymnosperms for conduction of water. In angiosperms, vessels are composite structure as these are formed by dissolution of end walls of row of cells i.e., vessels elements. So angiosperms, have more efficient system of conduction due to presence of vessels. Conduction of water by vessel elements is also known as ascent of sap. Water absorbed by roots, goes upward to replace the water loss by transpiration. The most accepted theory for ascent of sap is transpiration pull theory i.e., when water is lost by transpiration from the leaves, a tension is created in the xylem and due to this water absorbed by roots hair is passed through vessels to the leaves. The xylem parenchyma are mainly for storage function but sometimes help in conduction.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Companion cells in plants are associated with
questions.solution: The companion cells occur only in angiosperms where they accompany most sieve tube elements. Companion cell is a speciliased type of parenchyma cell which is closely associated in origin, position and function with sieve tube elements. These cells are living having abundant granular cytoplasm and a prominent elongated nucleus. Usually, the nuclei of the companion cell serve for the nuclei of the sieve tubes as they lack them. The companion cells do not contain starch. They live only so long as the sieve tube element with which they are associated and they are crushed with those cells. Longitudinal division of the mother cell of the sieve tube element forms the companion cells. One daughter cell becomes a companion cell and other sieve tube element.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Cork cambium results in the formation of cork which becomes impermeable to water due to the accumulation of
questions.solution: Cork cambium is a secondary lateral meristem that may arise from permanent living cells of hypodermis or outer cortex. It is composed of a single layer of meristematic cells. Its cells divide tangentially and periclinally towards the outer face and produce cork cells. These cells are compactly arranged and have thin cellulose walls in the beginning. As they mature there is a gradual loss of living matter and cells get elongated radially, vertically or tangentially. The cell walls become thick because of development of fatty substance called suberin, which is impervious to water.

questions.solution: A zone of inactive cells is present in the central part of the root apex called quiscent centre. It is a hemispherical region of inactive cells present in between the root cap and the active meristematic region of root apex. This zone contains several hundred cells which are characterized by having lower concentration of DNA, RNA and protein. The quiescent centre acts as reservoir of cells and becomes active whenever the previously active initials get damaged or during the establishment of the secondary roots.

Reason : Casparian strips in endodermis are suberized.
options: If both Assertion and Reason are true and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion
If both Assertion and Reason are true but the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion
If Assertion is true statement but Reason is false
if both Assertion and Reason are false statements
questions.solution: The apoplast is the system of adjacent cell walls which is continuous through the plant. As water evaporates from the mesophyll cell walls into the intercellular air spaces, tension develops in the continuous stream of water in the apoplast, and water is drawn through the walls in a mass flow by the cohesion of water molecules. When water moving through spaces in the cell wall reaches the endodermis, it's progress is stopped by a waterproof substance called suberin which is deposited in cell walls in the form of bands called casparian strips. Therefore water and solutes must pass through the cell surface membrane and into the cytoplasm of the cells of the endodermis.

Histogen theory for shoot apical meristem has been proposed by Hanstein (1870). It advocates that there are three distinct meristematic zones (layers) called dermatogen periblem and plerome. questions.q: Meristematic tissue in vascular bundle is
questions.solution: The cambium present between the xylem and phloem of vascular bundle is called vascular cambium. It is a lateral meristem that gives rise to secondary xylem and phloem and occurs in the form of a thin strip. Vascular cambium is also called fascicular cambium.

questions.q: In monocot roots which types of vascular bundles are found?
